name: Civil unrest
value: France strike day drew 100,000+ on 17 Nov
summary: France's 17 Nov strike day drew over 100,000 by official count; protests stayed largely peaceful, no deadly unrest found
state: A nationwide strike and protest day over pay and living costs in France on 17 Nov drew more than 100,000 people by official count, the latest in a run of union actions since October (Al Jazeera). Unions had united for nationwide strikes from 5 Nov (CP24, AP). No deaths were reported. Sustained protests keep Watch; searches on 20 Nov found no deadly nationwide unrest or major crackdown in a large country.
for_you: Strike days in France can disrupt trains, flights and schools at short notice. FCDO travel advice for France covers strikes and demonstrations.
rubric_hit: Watch: significant protests (France nationwide strike days, 17 Nov); no deadly nationwide unrest in a major country found

sources.title: Al Jazeera — More than 100,000 take part in France pay protests
CP24 (AP) — French unions join forces for nationwide strikes, increasing pressure on Macron's government

why: Mass protest and state crackdowns signal political fragility and can topple governments.
drivers: Cost of living, elections, corruption, repression, food and fuel prices.

rubric.alert: Deadly nationwide unrest or a state crackdown in a major country.
rubric.watch: Significant protests in several countries or deadly unrest in one.
rubric.normal: No deadly mass unrest in large countries.
